1. Document Overview & Knowledge Base Scope
This document is a synthetic internal knowledge repository for Nexora Dynamics Pvt. Ltd., a fictional mid-size
enterprise software company. It consolidates corporate identity, leadership, departments, products, technology
architecture, finance, sales, human resources, IT security, incident history, customer support procedures,
procurement, internal projects, roadmap, compliance and risk into a single structured reference artifact.
Purpose: To act as a realistic test corpus for RAG pipelines, LangChain and LangGraph retrievers, vector store
population, semantic search evaluation and AI agent context injection.
Scope: Company profile, org structure, product catalog, engineering standards, FY2025-26 financials, sales

Scope: Company profile, org structure, product catalog, engineering standards, FY2025-26 financials, sales
accounts, HR policy, security policy, incident postmortem, support SLAs, vendors, projects, OKRs, compliance
and risk registers, and a frequently asked questions section.
Intended Usage: Chunking experiments, top-k retrieval tests, hybrid search evaluation, reranker benchmarking,
citation and grounding checks, and question-answering evaluation sets.
Version: NDK-2026.09 — initial release, 28 September 2026.
Organization Strategy: Every numbered section is self-contained and repeats the entity name it describes, so a
chunk retrieved in isolation still carries enough context to be answered from.

6.2 Sahayak RAG Architecture
The Sahayak assistant uses a retrieval-augmented generation pipeline. Documents are ingested nightly and on
change events, split into chunks of roughly 500 tokens with 80 tokens of overlap, embedded, and stored in a
per-tenant pgvector collection. At query time the user question is embedded, the top 20 chunks are retrieved

per-tenant pgvector collection. At query time the user question is embedded, the top 20 chunks are retrieved
using hybrid search that combines BM25 keyword scores with cosine similarity, and a reranker narrows the set to
the best 5 chunks that are placed in the prompt.
• Embedding model: 768-dimensional multilingual sentence embeddings, self-hosted.
• Reranker: cross-encoder model, adds about 120 ms to each query.
• Generation: external large language model accessed through an internal gateway with prompt logging.
• Guardrails: answers must cite at least one retrieved chunk, otherwise the assistant says it does not know.
• Evaluation: a nightly regression suite of 1,200 question-answer pairs; target faithfulness score of 0.92.

11. Information Security Policy
This policy is owned by Chief Information Security Officer Kavya Nair and applies to all employees, contractors
and systems at Nexora Dynamics. It is reviewed annually and was last updated on 1 July 2026.
11.1 Access Control
• Access follows the principle of least privilege and is granted through role-based groups.
• Multi-factor authentication is mandatory for all corporate applications and production access.
• Privileged production access is granted just-in-time for a maximum of 4 hours and is fully logged.

• Privileged production access is granted just-in-time for a maximum of 4 hours and is fully logged.
• Access reviews are performed quarterly by system owners; unused access is removed after 45 days.
• Departing employees lose all access within 2 hours of their last working day being recorded.
11.2 Password and Device Rules
• Passwords must be at least 14 characters and are checked against breached-password lists.
• Company laptops use full-disk encryption and must receive security patches within 14 days of release.
• Personal devices may access email only through the managed mobile application.
• USB mass storage is disabled on all company laptops by default.

12.1 Postmortem — INC-2026-0417: Workflow Runtime Delay
Date: 17 April 2026, 02:14 to 05:52 IST
Severity: SEV1
Incident Commander: Sanjay Iyer
Customer Impact: Approximately 310 customers experienced workflow execution delays of up to 3 hours. No
data was lost.
Root Cause: A Kafka consumer group rebalance loop was triggered by a configuration change that lowered the
session timeout from 30 seconds to 6 seconds. Under a nightly batch load, consumers missed heartbeats,
repeatedly restarted and could not commit offsets.
Detection: Automated alert on consumer lag exceeding 500,000 messages fired at 02:19 IST.
Resolution: The session timeout was restored to 30 seconds and the consumer group was scaled from 12 to 20

Resolution: The session timeout was restored to 30 seconds and the consumer group was scaled from 12 to 20
pods to drain the backlog.
12.2 Corrective Actions
• Add a configuration validation rule that blocks session timeouts below 20 seconds (owner: Platform, done 30
April 2026).
• Require canary rollout for all Kafka configuration changes (owner: SRE, done 15 May 2026).
• Add consumer lag dashboards to the customer status page (owner: Reliability, done 10 June 2026).
• Run a quarterly game day simulating consumer failures (owner: SRE, first held 24 July 2026).
12.3 Incident Statistics for 2026 (January to August)
There were 2 SEV1 incidents, 9 SEV2 incidents and 41 SEV3 incidents. Mean time to detect was 4.6 minutes and
mean time to resolve for SEV1 and SEV2 incidents was 96 minutes.
